Exam Name: Screening Mammography, Bilateral with CAD

Reason for Exam / Clinical Indication: Routine screening mammogram; no specific breast complaints. Patient is 52 years old, due for annual screening.

Technique: Digital mammography was performed in craniocaudal (CC) and mediolateral oblique (MLO) projections of both breasts. Computer-aided detection (CAD) was applied.

Comparison Study: Prior mammogram dated 05/22/2023 (available for review).

Findings:
BREAST COMPOSITION: The breasts are heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses.
RIGHT BREAST: No suspicious masses, architectural distortion, or suspicious calcifications are identified. Skin and subcutaneous tissues are unremarkable.
LEFT BREAST: No suspicious masses, architectural distortion, or suspicious calcifications are identified. Skin and subcutaneous tissues are unremarkable.
AXILLAE: No axillary lymphadenopathy is noted bilaterally.
CAD ANALYSIS: No suspicious findings were highlighted by CAD.

Impression:
BI-RADS Category 1: Negative. No mammographic evidence of malignancy. Stable appearance compared to prior study.

Recommendation: Continue with routine annual screening mammography.
